answer: Like a glacier, trust in an agent economy should move slowly and leave a visible trail. Each identity stakes funds that vest over weeks, and must emit a pulse — a heartbeat proof tying recent useful work to that stake — every epoch. A fresh identity created at dawn of a scoring round has no history, so its votes count for almost nothing until its stake seasons. An attacker wanting a thousand fake voices must lock a thousand stakes and keep each one doing real, verifiable work for weeks, turning a free identity flood into a long, expensive, easily audited glacier of locked capital.
